REPORT

S.1 Special Branch File No. ____ Date August 29, 1941.

SUBJECT: Confidential communication dated 19-8-41
from the British Consulate-General concerning
12 Russians who wish to join the Allied
Forces

The following information is available regarding
the 12 Russians whose names and addresses are given in
the attached communication :-

(1) Anatole Joseph COROT (KOROTH), Russian Jew,
registered at the offices of the Russian Emigrants
Committee, Shanghai, was born in Irkutsk, Siberia,
on September 7, 1910. He received his education
at Liege University, Belgium, from whence he
graduated in economic science. In 1932 Corot
left Europe and came to Shanghai where he was
successful in obtaining a clerical position with
S.E. Levy & Company, Investment Bankers and Brokers.
He remained in Shanghai until 1937 when, in company
with R.O. Kopelman, he was sent as representative
of his firm to Singapore. He returned to Shanghai
some time in 1940. His present place of
employment is not known.
His father, Joseph R. KOROTH, who at one time was
suspected of having been employed by Soviet
Government as a political agent, absconded from
Shanghai in 1939 in order to escape his creditors.

(2) Victor Ivanovich NEVEROFF, Russian, born on
22-10-1912 in Tobolsk, Siberia. According to
his own statement, he resided in Manchuria from
1918 to September 1931, after which he came to
Shanghai. For the past several years he is
reported to have been employed with the French
Fire Brigade.
He is married and has a daughter, 3 years of age.

(3) Pavel Andreyevich KONDRATOFF, Russian, born on
12-5-1917 at Tomsk, Siberia. He is reported to
have resided in Manchuria from 1921 to 1935 when
he arrived in Shanghai. From 1-10-35 to 31-1-40
he served in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C., leaving
the service upon expiry of his agreement and with
a discharge certificate giving him a good
character. From 26-2-41 to 1-5-41 he was
employed as a bodyguard to a Chinese residing at
the Broadway Mansions and from 3-7-41 has been
employed in the same capacity with Cheu Fong Mah,
Chief of Income Tax Bureau, Ministry of Finance,
Nanking Government.
On 28-5-41 he was placed on the list of candidates
for the position of watchman and/or bodyguard
approved by the Shanghai Municipal Police.

(4). Evgeny Abramovitch KRINKEVITCH, Russian Jew, born
on 8-4-1913 at Irkutsk, Siberia. He is reported
to have left Russia for Manchuria in 1917. Upon

关于附函中所列姓名及地址的12名俄国人，现有如下信息：

(1) 阿纳托利·约瑟夫·科罗特（Anatole Joseph COROT）（亦作 KOROTH），俄罗斯犹太人，在上海俄国侨民委员会办公室登记注册，1910年9月7日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。他在比利时列日大学接受教育，并毕业于经济学专业。1932年，科罗特离开欧洲来到上海，成功在投资银行家与经纪人 S.E. Levy & Company 获得一份职员职位。他留在上海直至1937年，当时他与 R.O. Kopelman 一同被其公司派往新加坡担任代表。他于1940年的某个时候返回上海。目前他的受雇地点不详。
其父约瑟夫·R·科罗斯（Joseph R. KOROTH）曾一度被怀疑受苏联政府雇用充当政治代理人，为躲避债权人于1939年从上海潜逃。

(2) 维克多·伊万诺维奇·涅韦罗夫（Victor Ivanovich NEVEROFF），俄罗斯人，1912年10月22日出生于西伯利亚托博尔斯克。据其自述，他于1918年至1931年9月期间居住在满洲，之后来到上海。据报道，过去几年他受雇于法租界消防队。
他已婚，育有一名三岁的女儿。

(3) 帕维尔·安德烈耶维奇·孔德拉托夫（Pavel Andreyevich KONDRATOFF），俄罗斯人，1917年5月12日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克。据报道，他于1921年至1935年间居住在满洲，随后抵达上海。从1935年10月1日至1940年1月31日，他在上海义勇军（S.V.C.）俄国连服役，合约期满后离职，并获得一份证明其品行良好的退伍证书。从1941年2月26日至1941年5月1日，他受雇担任一名居住于百老汇大厦的中国人的保镖；自1941年7月3日起，他以同样身份受雇于南京政府财政部所得税局局长周丰马（Cheu Fong Mah，音译）。
1941年5月28日，他被列入经上海公共租界工部局警务处批准的巡捕和/或保镖职位候选人名单。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

Special Branch ............Station. File No.................... Date August 24, 1942.

SUBJECT: Confidential communication dated 13-8-41 from
the British Consulate-General concerning 23
Russians who wish to join the Allied Forces.

The following information is available regard-
ing the 23 individuals whose names and addresses are gi-
ven in the attached communication:-

(1) Peter Trofimovich IVANOFF, Russian, born on
27-5-1908 at Ekaterinoslav, South Russia. According to
his own statement, he escaped from the U.S.S.R. to Manchu-
ria in 1930 and in September of the same year arrived in
Shanghai. Here he is known to have worked as a splicer
with the Shanghai Telephone Co. on two occasions ( from
January to July, 1931 and from August, 1937 to September,
1938 ) and also as an acrobat with different companies
of entertainers appearing in local theatres and cabarets.
In 1931, 1934 and 1935 he made unsuccessful starts from
Shanghai on a round-the-world trip in company with ano-
ther Russian named M. Kuznetsoff, each time returning to
Shanghai after a short period of absence. In October,
1938 he departed from Shanghai together with a group of
Russians in a sailing boat heading for Manila. Owing to
bad weather they were forced to enter a port at Formosa
where they were arrested by the Japanese authorities on
suspicion of espionage. After 4 months' detention they
were allowed to continue their trip and eventually reach-
ed Manila where the group broke up. Ivanoff returned to
Shanghai in August, 1939. On 7-2-40 he joined the Russian
Detachment, S.V.C., but resigned after three weeks' service
in order to join the French Foreign Legion and left for
Saigon in March of the same year. He returned here in
March, 1941 and has since been without fixed employment.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / AUG 26 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

(2) Sender Leibovich BOR, Russian of Jewish ori-
gin, born on 13-12-1920 at Harbin. He is reported to have
arrived in Shanghai in March, 1938 from Tientsin where he
resided for many years and attended a school. Here he has
been residing with his parents without any fixed employ-
ment. His father is the proprietor of the Gloria Cafe,
542/3 Avenue Joffre.

(3) Avraam Alexandrovich MARKEVITCH, Russian, born
on 28-10-1919 at Nikolsk-Ussouriysk, Maritime Province,
Russia. According to his own statement, he left the U.S.S.R
for Manchuria in 1928 and subsequently resided in Harbin
where he attended the Y.M.C.A. High School for about 5
years. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin some time in
1933. Here he is reported to have been employed with
Wills Motors for about 2½ years, the Russian Auxiliary De-
tachment, French Police, for a period and with the Shanghai
Gas Company.

(4) Alexander Carolevich LEVKOVITCH, Russian, born
on 2-9-1918 at Harbin. He claims to have graduated from
the Y.M.C.A. High School at Harbin in 1935 and from the
Harbin Polytechnic Institute ( Electrical Engineering

特别警察科 ____ 分局。档案号 ____ 日期：1942年8月24日。

主题：英国总领事馆于1941年8月13日发出的机密函件，涉及23名希望加入盟军的俄国人。

关于附件函件中列明姓名和地址的23人，现有如下信息：

(1) 彼得·特罗菲莫维奇·伊万诺夫（Peter Trofimovich IVANOFF），俄国人，1908年5月27日出生于南俄罗斯叶卡捷琳诺斯拉夫（Ekaterinoslav）。据其自述，他于1930年从苏联逃往满洲，并于同年9月抵达上海。据悉，他曾两次在上海电话公司担任接线员（1931年1月至7月，以及1937年8月至1938年9月），并曾在当地剧院和歌舞厅演出的不同娱乐团体中担任杂技演员。1931年、1934年和1935年，他与另一名名为M.库兹涅佐夫（M. Kuznetsoff）的俄国人结伴，三次尝试从上海出发进行环球旅行，但每次均在短暂离开后返回上海。1938年10月，他与一群俄国人乘帆船离开上海前往马尼拉。由于天气恶劣，他们被迫进入台湾的一个港口，在那里因涉嫌间谍活动被日本当局逮捕。在被拘留4个月后，他们获准继续行程，最终抵达马尼拉，随后该团体解散。伊万诺夫于1939年8月返回上海。1940年2月7日，他加入上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄国分队，但在服役三周后辞职，以便加入法国外籍军团，并于同年3月前往西贡。他于1941年3月返回此处，此后一直无固定职业。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 8月26日 / 特别警察科）

(2) 森德尔·莱博维奇·博尔（Sender Leibovich BOR），犹太裔俄国人，1920年12月13日出生于哈尔滨。据报，他于1938年3月从天津抵达上海，此前他在天津居住多年并就读于一所学校。在此地，他与父母同住，无固定职业。其父是霞飞路542/3号格洛丽亚咖啡馆（Gloria Cafe）的业主。

(3) 阿夫拉姆·亚历山德罗维奇·马尔克维奇（Avraam Alexandrovich MARKEVITCH），俄国人，1919年10月28日出生于俄罗斯滨海省乌苏里斯克尼古拉耶夫斯克（Nikolsk-Ussouriysk）。据其自述，他于1928年离开苏联前往满洲，随后居住在哈尔滨，并在基督教青年会中学就读约5年。他于1933年间从哈尔滨抵达上海。据悉，他在此曾受雇于威尔斯汽车公司（Wills Motors）约两年半，曾在法国警察所属的俄国辅助分队服役一段时间，并曾在上海煤气公司工作。

(4) 亚历山大·卡罗列维奇·列夫科维奇（Alexander Carolevich LEVKOVITCH），俄国人，1918年9月2日出生于哈尔滨。他声称于1935年毕业于哈尔滨基督教青年会中学，并毕业于哈尔滨工业大学（电气工程

It appears that his parents were divorced in or about 1931,following which his mother married one K.F.Cole,American,who subsequently gave his name to his step-son. Prior to his coming to Shanghai some time in 1939 G.Cole resided in Harbin ( until 1931 ), Tsingtao (1931-1934 and 1936-1938 ) and Tientsin ( 1934-1936 ). In the latter city he is reported to have attended the St.Louis College for two years. Following his arrival in Shanghai he is reported to have been employed as an apprentice at the Yee Tsoong Tobacco Co., Pootung.
His mother,Mrs C.M.Cole is believed to be in America at present ( 2068 Sutter Street,San Francisco ) and his step-father is reported to be employed at a tobacco factory in Tsingtao.

(6). Anatoly Yakovlevich VVEDENSKY,Russian,born on 6-7-1913 at Harbin. According to his own statement, he escaped from the U.S.S.R. to Manchuria in 1921. From 1923 to 1925 he resided in Hankow with his parents,after which he arrived in Shanghai. Here he attended the French Municipal College for several years and upon leaving the college is known to have been employed with the French Power Company in 1934-1935. In September,1935 he opened a small business of his own - a radio repairing shop at 66/29 Rue Lorton. He is also reported to have attended the Wireless Courses of the Russian Mercantile Marine Association,12 Rue du Consulat, for a period. Particulars regarding his employment for the past several years are not available.

(7). Mihail Froimovich KESSEL,Russian of Jewish origin,born on 7-1-1920 at Tiraspol,South Russia. He is reported to have left the U.S.S.R. for Manchuria in 1931 together with his mother and after a short stay in Harbin proceeded to Shanghai. Towards the end of 1932 he left for Tientsin where he attended the St.Louis College until 1937. For the following two years he studied at the Y.M.C.A.Business College in Harbin. Returning to Shanghai in November,1939 he was without fixed employment until August,1940 when he was engaged as a meter inspector by the Shanghai Gas Co.

(6). 阿纳托利·雅科夫列维奇·韦杰缅斯基（Anatoly Yakovlevich VVEDENSKY），俄国人，1913年7月6日出生于哈尔滨。据其自述，他于1921年从苏联逃往满洲。1923年至1925年间，他与父母居住在汉口，随后抵达上海。在此地，他就读于法公董局学校（French Municipal College）数年，离校后，已知他于1934-1935年间受雇于法商电力公司（French Power Company）。1935年9月，他在罗登路（Rue Lorton）66/29号开设了一家自己的小店铺——无线电修理店。另据报，他曾一度参加位于领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）12号的俄国商船协会（Russian Mercantile Marine Association）举办的无线电课程。关于其过去几年的就业详情，暂无资料可查。

(7). 米哈伊尔·弗罗伊莫维奇·凯塞尔（Mihail Froimovich KESSEL），犹太裔俄国人，1920年1月7日出生于南俄罗斯蒂拉斯波尔（Tiraspol）。据报，他于1931年与母亲一同离开苏联前往满洲，在哈尔滨短暂停留后前往上海。1932年底，他前往天津，并在圣路易斯学院（St.Louis College）就读至1937年。随后的两年，他在哈尔滨的基督教青年会商学院（Y.M.C.A.Business College）学习。1939年11月返回上海后，他一直处于无固定职业状态，直到1940年8月被上海煤气公司（Shanghai Gas Co.）聘为抄表员。

(8). 鲍里斯·米哈伊洛维奇·兰金（Boris Mihailovich LANKIN），俄国人，1919年3月6日出生于西伯利亚阿穆尔州布拉戈维申斯克（Blagoveschensk）。据其自述，他从幼年起至1931年居住在哈尔滨，随后的八年居住在沈阳和青岛。他就读于沈阳的一所俄国学校，并声称拥有无线电机械师的一些经验。他于1940年1月从青岛抵达上海，同年3月进行了一次不寻常的……

mi, being supported by his parents who are believed to
be in Harbin at present.

(9). 彼得·彼得罗维奇·阿加波夫（Petr Petrovich AGAPOFF），俄国人，1896年6月12日出生于俄国奥伦堡（Orenbourg）。他自称出身于奥伦堡哥萨克部队的一名哥萨克，声称曾于1914年毕业于基辅的一所俄国中学，并于1916年毕业于海军军官航空学校。他自称为飞行员，并声称曾在俄国陆军和海军中以此身份服役。据报他于1924年离开俄国前往满洲，随后居住在中国多个城镇，包括奉天、天津、烟台、济南府和青岛，推测是从事其专业工作。他在1935年之前曾多次访问上海，且已知在过去几年中一直居住在上海。据报他在此期间曾受雇于一家中国公司担任看守一段时间，并自1940年9月起受雇于上海自来水公司。

(14) Constantin Ivanovich ZNAMINSKY, Russian,
born in 1895 at St. Petersburg, Russia. According to his
own statement, he graduated from a commercial school at
Yamburg and afterwards studied mathematics and physics
at the University of St. Petersburg from 1912 to 1916, at
the same time following a course in the metallurgy at
the Polytechnic Institute in the same city. In 1915 he
joined the army as a volunteer and in August of the same
year was sent to the Irkutsk Military School. Upon gradu-
ating in 1916 he served in the army until April, 1917.
During the civil war in Siberia he was attached to the
Military Intelligence Department at Omsk and from 1919
to 1920 served in Ataman Semenoff's army in Chita, Trans-
baikal Province. In 1921-1922 he served in the white
forces in Vladivostok first being attached to the Mili-
tary Intelligence & Counter-Espionage Service and later
to a technical unit of that army. From 1923 to 1934 he
resided at Harbin working as a teacher of mathematics.
He claims to have been engaged during that period in po-
litical intelligence work on behalf of General Gondatti,
the exact nature of the work being unknown.
Znamensky arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in March, 1934
and lived without fixed employment and in very straite-
ned circumstances until 1935 when he secured the posi-
tion of a teacher of drawing in the St. Joan of Arc's
College. It appears that in 1933-1934 he made a trip to
Japan where he endeavoured to sell an alleged invention
of his, but without success. In Shanghai he is reported
to have made unsuccessful efforts to interest the Japa-
nese and American consulates in his invention. According
to Russian newspapers reports dating to September, 1938,
the invention in question is an improvement in the con-
struction of motor boats.
Leaving his position in the St. Joan of Arc's College
some time in 1937 he has since been residing at 333/3
Baikal Road, where he is reported to have conducted his
own workshop and also classes of technical knowledge.
In July 1937 he made an unsuccessful application for a
position in the Special Branch, S.M.Police.
Some persons, who know Znamensky, describe him as a ner-
vous and rather mentally unbalanced individual which,
probably, is the result of the hardships he is reported
to have experienced in the past. He is married and has
three children.

1937 he was absent to Tientsin and Hankow, returning here
in January, 1938. In July, 1939 he was engaged by the
Globe Wireless Co, but was dismissed later in the same
year on account of his laziness and inefficiency. He
is not known to have any steady employment here and is
reported to be supported by his sisters, of whom one is

(14) 康斯坦丁·伊万诺维奇·兹纳明斯基（Constantin Ivanovich ZNAMINSKY），俄国人，
1895年生于俄罗斯圣彼得堡。据其自述，他毕业于扬堡（Yamburg）的一所商业学校，随后于1912年至1916年在圣彼得堡大学学习数学和物理，同时在该市的理工学院修读冶金学课程。1915年，他志愿参军，同年8月被派往伊尔库茨克军事学校。1916年毕业后，他在军队服役至1917年4月。在西伯利亚内战期间，他隶属于鄂木斯克军事情报部，并于1919年至1920年在后贝加尔省赤塔的谢苗诺夫（Ataman Semenoff）阿塔曼军队中服役。1921年至1922年，他在符拉迪沃斯托克的白军部队中服役，起初隶属于军事情报与反间谍部门，后来隶属于该军队的技术单位。1923年至1934年，他居住在哈尔滨，担任数学教师。他声称在此期间曾为贡达蒂将军（General Gondatti）从事政治情报工作，但工作的具体性质不详。
兹纳明斯基于1934年3月从哈尔滨抵达上海，在没有固定职业且生活非常拮据的情况下度日，直到1935年他在圣女贞德学院（St. Joan of Arc's College）获得了一份绘图教师的职位。据悉，他在1933-1934年间曾前往日本，试图出售一项据称是其发明的成果，但未获成功。在上海，据报道他曾试图引起日本和美国领事馆对其发明的兴趣，但均未成功。根据1938年9月的俄文报纸报道，该项发明是对摩托艇构造的改进。
他于1937年的某个时候辞去了在圣女贞德学院的职务，此后一直居住在贝加尔路333/3号，据报道他在那里开设了自己的车间，并讲授技术知识课程。1937年7月，他申请加入上海公共租界警务处特别支部（Special Branch, S.M.Police），但未获录用。
一些认识兹纳明斯基的人形容他是一个神经质且精神相当不平衡的人，这可能是由于据报道他过去所经历的苦难所致。他已婚，育有三个孩子。

ZABAL ),Russian, born on 7-10-1917 at Station Bukhedu,

watchman at the Harbin Yacht Club. During the summer

JOHN JOSEPH HOLLAND.

John Joseph Holland is a British Subject, believed
to be Australian born, age 32 years, height about 5' 7", dark
hair turning grey, medium build, small dark moustache.

He first arrived in Shanghai from Hongkong during
1937 and claimed to have been the Hongkong correspondent of
the Sydney Daily Telegraph. He first made a living in
Shanghai as a free-lance journalist and was in fact what is
known in journalistic circles as a "runner", i.e. a person
who obtains and writes stories for local correspondents of
foreign newspapers. He failed to register at H.B.M. Consulate
on his arrival here, and he first came to the notice of the
S.M. Police in November 1939 when the Passport Officer at
H.B.M.'s Consulate asked the Police to endeavour to locate
this man as they had received a communication from the
Hongkong Government to the effect that a Maintenance Order
had been issued against him by the Court Authorities in Sydney
N.S.W. Australia, on the complaint of his wife Doris Emily
Muriel Holland. Although it was established that Holland was
in Shanghai, he could not be located at that time.

On March 1st 1941 J.J. Holland called on Mr. Beaurey,
Vice-Consul for France in charge of the Chancery and proposed
selling to the Government of Indo-China, seven bombers, which
according to Holland, were at that time in Manila. It appears
that Mr. Beaurey gave Holland no definite answer and later had
pages.zh:
机密

1941年3月11日。

（批：*亦见档案:-
D 9532(6)
E 32...）

JOHN JOSEPH HOLLAND。

John Joseph Holland 是英国臣民，据信出生于澳大利亚，年龄32岁，身高约5英尺7英寸，黑发渐灰，中等身材，留有黑色小胡子。

他于1937年间首次从香港抵达上海，并声称曾任悉尼《每日电讯报》的香港通讯员。他在上海起初以自由撰稿记者为生，实际上是新闻界所谓的“跑腿记者”，即为外国报纸的本地通讯员获取素材并撰写报道的人。他抵达此处后未在英国驻华领事馆登记，直到1939年11月才引起上海公共租界警务处的注意，当时英国驻华领事馆护照官员请求警方设法 locating 此人，因为他们收到香港政府来函，称澳大利亚新南威尔士州悉尼的法院当局已因其妻子 Doris Emily Muriel Holland 的投诉对他发出了赡养费令。虽然当时已查明 Holland 在上海，但未能找到其下落。

1941年3月1日，J.J. Holland 拜访了负责馆务的法国副领事 Beaurey 先生，提议向印度支那政府出售七架轰炸机，据 Holland 称，这些轰炸机当时在马尼拉。看来 Beaurey 先生并未给 Holland 明确答复，随后让

pages.en:
- 2 -

the French Police make enquiries regarding him and on finding
that he was associated with the firm "American Exporters", the
manager of which is an American Jew named Louis I. Raisin, who
is known to have close connections with the Japanese, the
French formed the opinion that Holland probably had no bombers
for sale and was only attempting to place the French
Authorities in a-n awkward position with the Japanese.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

法国警察对他进行调查，发现他与“美国出口商”（American Exporters）公司有关联，该公司经理是一名名叫 Louis I. Raisin 的美国犹太人，众所周知此人与日本人有密切关系，因此法国方面认为 Holland 可能并没有轰炸机可卖，只是试图使法国当局在日本人面前陷入尴尬境地。

CONFIDENTIAL

July 20, 1940.

^ Robert Sandeman Lamb (British).

*See also N250

Robert Sandeman Lamb (British) is reported
to have served as a junior officer in the Indian
Army or Air Force during the Great War. After
the Great War he is reported to have been
in Canada and the U.S.A., where he worked for
General Motors. From U.S.A., he is stated to have
gone to Japan where he also worked for General Motors.
Sometime prior to 1934, he came to Shanghai where he
subsisted precariously for some time. In 1936 he
was employed as business manager of the Cathay
Cosmopolitan, a monthly publication, the aims of
which were claimed to be the "provision of an
"independent forum for the expression of opinions
"on all manner of subjects pertaining to the economic,
"political and commercial life of this great
"community."

Associated with Lamb in this publication
were George M. Battey (American) Editor; Ian Black
Douglas, Associate Editor. Other contributors to
the publication were Mario Rocchi; Angius J.M. Herba
and Paul Paelz. Paul Paelz subsequently became a
pages.zh:
机密

1940年7月20日。

^ Robert Sandeman Lamb（英国人）。

*另见 N250

据报，Robert Sandeman Lamb（英国人）曾在大战期间担任印度陆军或空军的初级军官。大战结束后，据报他曾在加拿大和美国工作，在那里他为通用汽车公司工作。据说他从美国去了日本，在那里也为通用汽车公司工作。1934年之前的某个时候，他来到上海，在此艰难谋生了一段时间。1936年，他被聘为《华夏环球》（Cathay Cosmopolitan）月刊的业务经理，该刊宣称其宗旨是“提供一个独立论坛，用以表达关于这个伟大社区的经济、政治和商业生活各方面问题的意见”。

与该刊物有关联的还有 George M. Battey（美国人）编辑；Ian Black Douglas，副编辑。该刊物的其他撰稿人包括 Mario Rocchi；Angius J.M. Herba 和 Paul Paelz。Paul Paelz 后来成为

pages.en:
- 2 -

partner of Lamb in the publication. According to
information obtained at time of the first appearance
of this monthly magazine (January 1936) it was
subsidized by the South Manchurian Railway, Maj.
General Tsogai of the Kwantung Army and Paul Paelz
who was alleged to have had access to the funds of
the German and Italian Legations. Note: Paul Paelz
is now known to be an active agent of the Nazi Party
in Shanghai.

Lamb was in 1935-6-7, a frequent contributor
of letters to " The People's Tribune" under the
pseudonym "Junius Sinicus." Perusal of these letters
reveals them to be mostly of the type that seeks
to expose rackets and social evils.

The Cathay Cosmopolitan ceased publication
after the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities in
1937. On August 6th 1937, a quarrel over a cheque
took place between Lamb and Paelz, in the office of
the Cathay Cosmopolitan, Room 521, 128 Museum Road,
which resulted in Lamb assaulting and injuring Paelz
to the extent that he had to be treated in the General
Hospital. Paelz, however, chose not to charge Lamb
as they had to wind up the business of the magazine.
At this time they shared a room in the New Asia Hotel.
On March 31st 1937, Lamb also came to the notice of
the Police in connection with a letter which he wrote
pages.zh:
- 2 -

Lamb 在该刊物中的合伙人。根据在该月刊首次发行时（1936年1月）获得的信息，该刊物由南满洲铁道株式会社、关东军 Tsogai 少将以及据称能接触德国和意大利公使馆资金的 Paul Paelz 提供资助。注：现已知 Paul Paelz 是纳粹党在上海的一名活跃特工。

Lamb 在1935-6-7年间，经常以笔名“Junius Sinicus”向《人民论坛报》（The People's Tribune）投稿信件。查阅这些信件可知，它们大多属于揭露敲诈勒索团伙和社会弊病的一类。

1937年中日敌对行动爆发后，《华夏环球》停刊。1937年8月6日，Lamb 和 Paelz 在博物馆路128号521室的《华夏环球》办公室因支票发生争吵，导致 Lamb 殴打并致伤 Paelz，使其不得不前往广慈医院接受治疗。然而，Paelz 选择不对 Lamb 提出指控，因为他们必须结束杂志的业务。当时他们合住在新华饭店的一个房间里。1937年3月31日，Lamb 还因写给他

pages.en:
- 3 -

to his former secretary, a Eurasian, Miss P.I.Ellison
(British) divorced wife of Mr. F.R.W.Barrett,
demanding the return of his bank passbook and a
cheque, which, it appears, Miss Ellison was holding
against a debt he owed her. The letter was couched
in terms which almost amounted to blackmail and
hinted that he was in possession of information
concerning the manner in which her divorce was
arranged, which might be of interest to the King's
Proctor, etc., etc. No Police action was taken
however as Miss Ellison wished to avoid publicity.
A charge of obtaining food and beverages
to .he value of $197.00 by means of false pretences,
preferred against Lamb in H.B.M. Court, Shanghai,
was dismissed on 6-12-34.
Lamb also came to the notice of the Police
on 30-8-35 when he assaulted and injured a public
ricsha coolie as a result of a dispute over payment
of fare. Lamb, however, paid compensation to the
coolie who withdrew the charge.
Lamb is known locally as a pugnacious, loud
mouthed individual, who talks glibly on almost any
subject. He refers to various Consular officials
and prominent business and professional men locally
as his intimate friends and gives the impression that
one or the other of these persons is pulling the
strings to get him a good job which is a certainty
pages.zh:
- 3 -

前任秘书、欧亚混血女士 P.I. Ellison 小姐（英国人，F.R.W. Barrett 先生的离异妻子）的一封信而引起警方注意，信中要求归还他的银行存折和一张支票，看来 Ellison 小姐扣留这些物品是为了抵偿他欠她的债务。这封信的措辞几乎构成敲诈勒索，并暗示他掌握有关她离婚安排方式的信息，这些信息可能会引起国王检察官等的兴趣等等。然而，由于 Ellison 小姐希望避免公开曝光，警方未采取行动。
Lamb 在上海英国法院被控以虚假手段骗取价值197.00元的食物和饮料，该指控于1934年12月6日被驳回。
Lamb 还于1935年8月30日引起警方注意，当时他因车费纠纷殴打并致伤一名公共人力车夫。然而，Lamb 向车夫支付了赔偿金，车夫撤回了指控。
Lamb 在当地被认为是一个好斗、大嗓门的人，几乎对任何话题都能夸夸其谈。他将各位领事官员和当地著名的商界及专业人士称为自己的亲密朋友，并给人留下这样的印象：这些人中的某一个正在幕后操纵，确信能为他弄到一份好工作

pages.en:
- 4 -

but the job never materializes and he glibly explains
the matter away by claiming that he is on the verge
of securing a much better situation. Among those
whom he frequently refers to in this manner are the
following :- Mr. W.J. Keswick, Mr. Ranald George
McDonald, Mr. A.F.T. Holland and Mr. R.S. Heaney,
former Passport & Registration Officer, H.B.M.
Consulate General.

Lamb has a habit of getting into debt but
usually succeeds, by means of his glib speech, in
getting one of his acquaintances to settle his
accounts. Despite his permanent lack of ready money,
he regularly contrives to get drunk but much of the
liquor he consumes he obtains by forcing his company
on casual acquaintances. As far as can be ascertained,
he has had no regular employment since 1937 but is
stated to have done casual jobs of accounting and
editing around the city.

Lamb was formerly a member of the Shanghai
Engineers Club, Room 500, 220 Szechmen Road but was
recently expelled, due to failure to pay his debts.
Through his membership of this club, he made the
acquaintance of Mr. F.A. Naylor, Secretary & Treasurer
of the Club. Late one night about the end of
September or beginning of October, 1939, he appeared
outside Naylor's flat, Room 704, 220 Szechmen Road
pages.zh:
- 4 -

但这份工作从未落实，他巧言令色地搪塞过去，声称自己即将获得一份好得多的职位。他经常以这种方式提及的人包括：W.J. Keswick 先生、Ranald George McDonald 先生、A.F.T. Holland 先生以及前英国驻华总领事馆护照与登记官 R.S. Heaney 先生。

Lamb 有负债的习惯，但通常能凭借其花言巧语，让某位熟人替他还清账目。尽管他长期缺乏现金，却定期设法喝醉，而他消费的许多酒水是通过强行纠缠泛泛之交而获得的。据查，自 1937 年以来他没有固定工作，但据说在市内从事过一些零散的会计和编辑工作。

Lamb 曾是上海工程师俱乐部（四川路 220 号 500 室）的成员，但最近因欠债不还而被开除。通过该俱乐部的会员身份，他结识了俱乐部秘书兼财务主管 F.A. Naylor 先生。1939 年 9 月底或 10 月初的一个深夜，他出现在 Naylor 位于四川路 220 号的公寓外

pages.en:
- 5 -

(Wayfoong House) covered in blood and mud and begging
to be admitted. His story was that he had become
involved in a fight with an Indian and that he was
without money and had been ordered out off the Navy
Y.M.C.A. for failure to pay his bills. As usual,
he had a plausible story of being on the point of
obtaining a good job from the China Printing and
Finishing Company, Ltd., which, needless to say,
never materialized. Naylor befriended Lamb and
allowed him to stay in his flat temporarily, in the
hope that he would get a job but the former has not
yet obtained work and is still living in Naylor's
flat despite repeated efforts by Naylor to eject him.
Recently, Naylor locked Lamb out and the latter made
a habit of coming back to Wayfoong House late at night,
drunk and sleeping outside Naylor's door. In
order to avoid embarrassment, Naylor has again admitted
Lamb to his flat on condition that he shall pull
himself together and make an effort to get work.
Lamb has been endeavouring to give Naylor the
impression that he is daily expecting advice from
the British Consulate to join H.M. Forces or take up
some other form of work. Lamb came home drunk both
on Wednesday night and Thursday night, July 17th and
18th 1940, which, in view of the fact that he is
pages.zh:
- 5 -

（汇中大楼 704 室），浑身是血和泥，乞求让他进去。他的说法是，他卷入了一场与一名印度人的斗殴，身无分文，并因未付账单被海军青年会（Navy Y.M.C.A.）勒令离开。像往常一样，他编造了一个看似合理的故事，称即将从中国印刷整理有限公司（China Printing and Finishing Company, Ltd.）获得一份好工作，当然，这从未实现。Naylor 对 Lamb 施以援手，允许他暂时住在自己的公寓里，希望他能找到工作，但前者至今仍未就业，尽管 Naylor 多次试图将他赶走，他仍住在 Naylor 的公寓里。最近，Naylor 将 Lamb 锁在门外，后者便养成习惯，深夜醉醺醺地回到汇中大楼，睡在 Naylor 的门外。为了避免尴尬，Naylor 再次允许 Lamb 进入其公寓，条件是他必须振作起来，努力找工作。Lamb 一直试图给 Naylor 留下这样的印象：他每天都在等待英国领事馆的通知，要么加入英王陛下军队，要么从事其他形式的工作。1940 年 7 月 17 日（星期三）和 18 日（星期四）晚上，Lamb 都醉酒回家，鉴于他

pages.en:
- 6 -

usually short of money, gives some colour to
information received, to the effect that he has
recently been receiving sums of money from a German.
H.E. Becker of Merck Chemical Co., who is a close
associate of S. Lahrman, prominent local Nazi. There
appears to be little doubt that Lamb is an unscrupulous
and dangerous individual who associates with all sorts
of people, including Germans. He is possessed of a
brilliant brain and a good education but appears
incapable of directing his ability to the best
purpose. Possessed of considerable debating ability,
he frequently took a prominent part in debates in the
Foreign Y. M. C. A. and in this manner widened his
circle of foreign acquaintances. Recently, he has
been endeavouring to cultivate the acquaintance of
foreign members of the S.M.P., his motive apparently
being mainly to obtain alcoholic drinks at the latter's
expense.

The S.M.P. have no record of the "Cathay Review"
as a successor to the "Cathay Cosmopolitan" and as
far as can be ascertained there is no such publication
on sale in Shanghai at the present time. It is
possible, however, that Lamb may be contemplating the
publication of such a periodical.
pages.zh:
- 6 -

通常缺钱的情况，这在一定程度上佐证了所收到的情报，即他最近从一名德国人那里收取款项。此人是默克化学公司（Merck Chemical Co.）的 H.E. Becker，他是当地纳粹分子 S. Lahrman 的亲密伙伴。毫无疑问，Lamb 是一个肆无忌惮且危险的人物，他与各色人等交往，包括德国人。他天资聪颖，受过良好教育，但似乎无法将自己的能力用于正途。他具备相当的辩论能力，经常在外侨青年会（Foreign Y. M. C. A.）的辩论中扮演重要角色，并以此扩大了其外籍熟人圈。最近，他一直试图结交工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的外籍成员，其动机显然主要是为了让人请客喝酒。

警务处没有“Cathay Review”作为“Cathay Cosmopolitan”继任刊物的记录，据查，目前上海也没有此类出版物在售。然而，Lamb 可能正考虑出版此类期刊。

REPORT

（手写批注：9411/19(3) 10 5- 48）

S. 1., Special Branch Station File No. ____ Date ____ MAY 9, 1941.

SUBJECT: Messrs. J.J. MARTIN and B. BEESLEY

With reference to the attached enquiry from
the British Consulate.

Mr. Jasper Joseph MARTIN, age 45, has been
employed by the Shanghai Water Works as a clerk for
the past 15 years, during this period of employment
his character has been exemplary. Nothing is known
in Police records to the detriment of Mr. MARTIN.

Mr. Basil BEESLEY, age 32, has been employed
by the Shanghai Telephone Company as an engineer for the
past 15 years and is considered by the Company to be
of excellent character. His position will be held open
for him until he returns to Shanghai. He has recently
been divorced from his wife although the decree is
not yet absolute. Nothing is known in Police records
to the detriment of Mr. BEESLEY.

（手写：b/a/s）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / MAY 9 1941 / ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER / SPECIAL BRANCH）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
（批：9411/19(e) J If #1）

S. 1, Special Branch Station. File No. ____ Date April 1, 1941.

SUBJECT:
J. J. Walsh

（批：x Au alu A J...）

J.J. Walsh, 43, British, residing Clements Apartments, 1363 Rue Lafayette, has been living in Shanghai for many years. By profession he is a Physical Training Instructor and Masseur. In this capacity he is extremely well-known locally and has a large and varied clientele. There have been many occasions however when he has been forced to rely on friends for sustenance. At present he has the appearance of being comparatively well-off.

J.J. Walsh came to Shanghai from Australia where, he has stated, he had been in the Police. There is no confirmation of this. It has been rumoured that he was a professional "card-sharper" in Australia but there is no evidence to hand to substantiate this. It is noted, however, that J.J. Walsh is exceedingly adept at card tricks and card players having a knowledge of this are known to refuse to join any card game in which he is a participant.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE APR 2 1941 SPECIAL BRANCH）

（批：3H 19 1/4）

J.J. Walsh came to the notice of the Police on June 28th, 1937 when he was involved in fight with one C.U. Putnam, American golf instructor, in a room at the Palace Hotel following a dispute over an alleged bridge debt. No Police action was taken.

There is nothing in Municipal Police records that could be construed as being detrimental to J.J. Walsh.
pages.zh:
FM. 2
G. 850-1-41

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
报告
（批注：9411/19(e) J If #1）

特务科第一分站。档案号 ____ 日期 1941年4月1日。

主题：
J. J. Walsh

（批注：x Au alu A J...）

J.J. Walsh，43岁，英国人，居住于拉斐特路1363号克莱门茨公寓，在上海已居住多年。职业为体育教练和按摩师。在此领域，他在本地极具知名度，拥有庞大且多样的客户群。然而，他多次不得不依靠朋友接济维持生计。目前看来，他的经济状况相对宽裕。

J.J. Walsh 来自澳大利亚，据称他曾在当地警察部门任职。此事未经证实。有传言称他在澳大利亚是一名职业“牌局作弊者”，但手头并无证据证实这一点。不过值得注意的是，J.J. Walsh 极其擅长纸牌戏法，知晓这一点的牌友通常拒绝参加有他在场的任何牌局。

（印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE APR 2 1941 SPECIAL BRANCH [上海公共租界警务处 1941年4月2日 特务科]）

（批注：3H 19 1/4）

J.J. Walsh 于1937年6月28日引起警方注意，当时他在华懋饭店（Palace Hotel）的一个房间内，因一笔所谓的桥牌债务纠纷，与美国高尔夫球教练 C.U. Putnam 发生斗殴。警方未采取行动。

在工部局警务处档案中，没有任何可被视为对 J.J. Walsh 不利的记录。

File No. __________
3. 1. Special Branch Statistics /
REPORT
Date February 28, 1941

Subject F.W.J. Barling

Made by D.F.S. Reynolds Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum

〔此处转录不清〕

F. W. J. Barling served for six years in the
1st Battalion Middlesex Regiment, after his discharge,
he joined the S. M. Police on November 17, 1927, but
was dismissed on July 16, 1929 for misconduct and
offences against Police discipline. He was employed
for a while by the China Realty Company but was dismissed
and subsequently departed for Vancouver, B.C.

Whilst living in Canada, Barling is believed to
have been convicted up to the end of 1931 twice for theft
and once for passing a worthless cheque. In April,
1934 he was stated to be serving 30 days imprisonment
in connection with the passing of a worthless cheque.
After this term of imprisonment expired Barling returned
to Shanghai, arriving on July, 19, 1934, he is believed
to have been deported.

Since his return to Shanghai Barling has been
concerned in several cases of passing worthless cheques
and fraud, in each of these cases however the
complainants declined to prosecute. From the beginning
of 1935 until the present time Barling has not come
to the notice of the Police, he is known to have been
acting as a barman or manager of various bars in
Chefoo and Shanghai but nothing further is known of his
movements during this period.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

A. C. (Special Branch)

G. U. Reynolds.
D. P. S.

〔此处转录不清〕

F. W. J. Barling 曾在米德尔塞克斯团（Middlesex Regiment）第1营服役六年，退役后，他于1927年11月17日加入上海公共租界工部局警务处（S. M. Police），但因行为不端及违反警队纪律，于1929年7月16日被开除。他曾被中国置业公司（China Realty Company）短暂雇用，但随后被解雇，之后前往不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华。

据信在加拿大居住期间，Barling 截至1931年底曾两次因盗窃罪被判刑，一次因开具空头支票被判刑。1934年4月，据称他因开具空头支票而被判处30天监禁。刑期届满后，Barling 返回上海，于1934年7月19日抵达，据信其已被驱逐出境。

自返回上海以来，Barling 卷入数起开具空头支票及欺诈案件，但在这些案件中，控告人均拒绝提起诉讼。从1935年初至今，Barling 未引起警方注意，已知他在烟台和上海担任多家酒吧的酒保或经理，但在此期间他的其他行踪不详。

（印：特别处）

A. C. (特别处)

G. U. Reynolds.
D. P. S.

（左侧页边椭圆印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE ... 26 1941 ... SPECIAL BRANCH）

Bertram John Deitz, British Eurasian,
was born at Shanghai on February 3, 1918.
He attended the Public & Thomas Hanbury
School until 1934 and then underwent a period of
commercial training. From June 1935 until
March 1936, he was employed at Messrs. Harking
Import & Export Company, 640 Avenue Foch but
left owing to staff reduction. He then
obtained employment as a clerk in the Cable
Department of Messrs. White, White & Company,
Brokers, 45 Kiukiang Road, where he is still
employed.

Nothing is known to his detriment and
he has not come to the attention of the Municipal
Police in any undesirable manner.

B.J. Deitz applied to join the S.M.P.
Specials on February 13, 1939 but was not
accepted as he was under age.

Special Branch ____ Station,

Date February 24, 1941

Subject Werner FALK, German Jewish refugee - Communication dated February
12, 1941 from H.B.M. Consulate-General

Made by D.S.I. Pitts Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum.

Werner FALK, German Jewish refugee, born in
Berlin on July 15, 1899, arrived in Shanghai from
Hamburg in the ss. Usaramo on June 28, 1939.
FALK speaks good though halting English but
more practice in this tongue would quickly enable
him to talk with facility on any subject. He
graduated from Berlin University in 1923 as a
diplomaed engineer, the English equivalent of which
would appear to approximate to Bachelor of Mechanical
Science. He has worked as a consulting and
designing engineer in several large German factories
and from 1928 until 1933 was with the well-known concern
of A.E.G. in Berlin as a designer of tools and special
mechanical machines. He was forced to leave this
organization in 1933 when Hitler first ordered his
anti-Jewish edicts. From 1933 onwards he perfected
a number of machines utilized for the spinning of
different types of yarn and at present in Shanghai
he is engaged in a small way in the manufacture of
yarn on machines he has designed and constructed
himself. This factory - a small one - is located
at 42/781 Tongshan Road.
He is married and resides with his wife (born
a Czechoslovakian, but now German by marriage) at
3/799 Tongshan Road.
He leads a very quiet life and is well spoken
of as being a capable type of individual. His
references have been seen and they speak of him and

Special Branch D.1 Station,
REPORT
Date January 25, 1941

Subject J. V. F. SPINK - Communication from British Consulate-General

Made by D.S.I. Litts Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to the contents of the communication dated January 20, 1941 from H.B.M. Consulate-General the applicant in question J. V. F. SPINK, Australian, states that he has never utilized the name of the A.C. (Special Branch) as a reference.

He arrived in Shanghai in 1927 and shortly afterwards secured a post with Messrs. Thomson & Co., Chartered Accountants, 20 Canton Road, as a bookkeeper. His services were satisfactory until 1936 when he had to resign due to the fact that he was in debt.

Since the time of his employment with Messrs. Thomson & Co., SPINK has earned his living by teaching English to organized classes. He has acted as English teacher to the ex-Russian Regiment, S.V.C. and to the University of Shanghai. More recently he has been attached to the Commercial Faculty teaching staff of the latter organization's in Yuen Ling Yuen Road.

Apart from the fact that he was in debt some five years ago - debts which it appears he has liquidated - nothing is known by this office to SPINK'S detriment.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 387/41）

Cox

A. C. (Special Branch).

D.S.I.

pool, Co. Durham, England.

From 10th January 1921 to 16th March 1926,
applicant served as a Private and Corporal in the 1st
Bat. East Yorkshire Regiment of the British Army, part
of which time he served with the Forces in Egypt and
Tientsin, China.

He purchased his discharge from the Army in
Tientsin on March 16th 1926 with a "Very Good" character
and on April 13th, 1926 obtained employment with Chinese
Maritime Customs as a Probationary Tide-Waiter.

Applicant left the Chinese Maritime Customs
service and joined the Shanghai Municipal Police as a
Probationary Sergeant on 21st February 1927.

His service in the Police Force was unsatisfactory
resulting in his dismissal on 11th December 1929.

The following is a brief resume of his career
after leaving the Police Force :-

December 11th 1929 to June 30th 1930 - unemployed.

July 1st 1930 to October 2nd 1930

Worked on the staff of Mr. B. Lennox Simpson, at Tientsin,
on the "seizure by Politico-Military Force of the Tientsin
Customs". Left that employment following death of
Mr. Simpson and disbandment of his organization.

呈报人：副督察长 威尔科克斯 (Wilcox)。转呈人：D. I. 克劳福德 (Crawford)。

约翰·H·托马斯 (John H. Thomas)，英国人，1903年5月8日出生于
英格兰达勒姆郡 (Co. Durham) 西哈特尔浦 (West Hartlepool)，
系埃文·J·托马斯 (Evan J. Thomas) 之子，住址为英格兰达勒姆郡
西哈特尔浦伍德街24号。

1921年1月10日至1926年3月16日期间，
申请人在英国陆军东约克郡团 (East Yorkshire Regiment) 第1营
服役，军衔从列兵升至下士，期间部分时间在埃及
和中国天津的部队中服役。

1926年3月16日，他在天津花钱买断军籍退伍，
品行评定为“很好”，并于1926年4月13日在中国海关
获得试用验货员 (Probationary Tide-Waiter) 的职位。

申请人离开中国海关服务部门，于1927年2月21日
加入上海公共租界工部局警务处，任试用巡长。

他在警队中的表现令人不满，导致其于1929年12月11日被开除。

以下是其离开警队后的履历简述：

1929年12月11日至1930年6月30日 - 失业。

1930年7月1日至1930年10月2日

在天津受雇于 B. 伦诺克斯·辛普森 (B. Lennox Simpson) 先生麾下，
参与“政治军事力量接管天津海关”事宜。随着
辛普森先生去世及其组织解散，他离开了该职位。

（左侧印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特科，内有签名及日期 41年1月22日）

November 1930 to February 1931 - unemployed.
March 1st 1931 to June 30th 1931 -
    Employed by Messrs Anderson, Meyers Co., Shanghai, as
a Refrigerator Salesman on Commission basis.
    Left voluntarily on finding himself inefficient
as a salesman due to general incompatability with
this type of work.
June 1931 to October 1931 - unemployed.
November 1st 1931 to July 1932 -
    Joined National Flood Relief Commission and took charge
of all Commissionary work in Kiangse and parts of
Anhwei and Hupeh, with headquarters at Kiukiang.
Was responsible for disbursement of funds and grain.
    Left on completion of work in areas stated and
has excellent testimonials from Sir John Hope Simpson
and Mr. John Carl Baker.
    Following a further period of unemployment in
March 1933 Applicant sought employment on the gaol
staff of the Shanghai Municipal Police, but his
application was not approved.
    From February 1934 to February 1938 applicant was
employed by the "Shanghai Society for the Prevention
of Cruelty to Animals", during which period his services
are believed to have been satisfactory.
